3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The House of Delegates was silent, a stark contrast to its former days of bustling activity.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: As I walked through the grand chamber, my gaze fell over the now-empty rows of seats.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Lucita walked beside me, her fingers trailing lightly along the edge of a nearby table.

6.speaker: Player_Romus
6.text: "The Delegates who once filled these seats claimed to represent the people, but they stood in defiance of the Crown’s will."

7.speaker: Lucita Azaro
7.text: "Thanks to you, those voices no longer trouble us."

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "They twisted our laws and traditions to suit their own ends."

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "It pains me to know that it came to this, but I did what needed to be done."

10.speaker: Player_Romus
10.text: "I couldn't allow them to steer our kingdom off course."

11.speaker: Lucita Azaro
11.text: "You've always done everything in your power to protect and uphold the integrity of these lands."

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "It’s a system that thrives on chaos and pandering to the lowest common denominator."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "A noble cause, but fraught with manipulation, discord, and empty promises."

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "It's like handing a child a hammer -- everything becomes a nail ready to be smashed into oblivion."

17.speaker: Lucita Azaro
17.text: "It only serves to destabilize and divide.”

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: Lucita smiled and placed a hand on my arm.

19.speaker: Lucita Azaro
19.text: "You've restored Rizia to its rightful place.”

20.speaker: Lucita Azaro
20.text: "...nothing and nobody will stand in our way."
20.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseToras_Conquered"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseSazon_Conquered"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Diplomacy_Intermerkopum"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_TerritorialIntegrity_Reclaimed"] == true) == false)

21.speaker: Lucita Azaro
21.text: "We've laid the foundations of a dynasty that will last a thousand years. More."

22.speaker: Lucita Azaro
22.text: "This room may be empty now, but it's full of promise."

23.speaker: Player_Romus
23.text: "We will build something enduring. As sovereign of this nation, I will not rest until my very last breath."

25.speaker: Lucita Azaro
25.text: "Well... we could turn the empty House into an elite boarding school reserved only for the children of our most powerful families."

27.speaker: Lucita Azaro
27.text: "We’d be ensuring the next generation of leaders are fully aligned with our vision for Rizia."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "Now that’s an idea. Cultivating the minds of the future right under our roof."

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "I don’t know… The children of the powerful can be difficult to control… but perhaps if done right, it could be useful."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: "Hah. Imagine the parents, clamoring to secure a spot for their precious offspring."

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Lucita and I walked deeper into the chamber.

32.speaker: Lucita Azaro
32.text: "Another option... we could create a Museum of History. A monument to Rizian heritage."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "And an opportunity to control the narrative by emphasizing the legitimacy of my rule."

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "Better yet, we could add a Hall of Traitors --  featuring the names and faces of every Delegate who opposed me."

36.speaker: Lucita Azaro
36.text: "Careful, there. It could just as easily turn into a Hall of Fame for the revolutionaries' acolytes."

37.speaker: Lucita Azaro
37.text: "Not as useful as a military hub, but it would serve as a reminder of where true power lies."

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: Lucita paused, taking in the statues of Rizian military figures that lined the hall.

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "Hope is merely the beginning. Soon, our populace will understand the guidance only a monarch can provide."

40.speaker: Player_Romus
40.text: "It's a new beginning, yes. But one that carries the weight of all we've sacrificed to get here."

41.speaker: Player_Romus
41.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] >= 1  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Lucita_DiscussedStratocracy"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Path_Stratocracy"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.War_Pales_Loss"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Overwhelming"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Strong"] == true)) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Path_Stratocracy"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.War_Pales_Loss"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Overwhelming"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Strong"] == true)) == false)

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: "But enough talk. We need to decide what to do with this piece of prime real estate."
42.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Resources_Budget"] >= 1  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Lucita_DiscussedStratocracy"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Path_Stratocracy"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.War_Pales_Loss"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Overwhelming"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Strong"] == true)) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Path_Stratocracy"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.War_Pales_Loss"] == false  and  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Overwhelming"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_PowerProjection_Strong"] == true)) == false)

44.speaker: Player_Romus
44.text: "We already have enough museums cluttering the city. Another one won’t change anything."

45.speaker: Player_Romus
45.text: "This chamber was a place where the old order clung to power. But now, it’s ours to reshape."

46.speaker: Player_Romus
46.text: "This hall stands as a testament to the Crown's true strength. They spoke and argued, but in the end, I prevailed."

47.speaker: Lucita Azaro
47.text: "They didn't see the future you envisioned."

48.speaker: Lucita Azaro
48.text: "History will remember this as the moment you secured your place -- *our* place -- in Rizia’s legacy."

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: "Establishing a national defense headquarters is essential. Without question." [-3 Budget]

50.speaker: Player_Romus
50.text: "I believe establishing an elite boarding school would best serve the kingdom." [-1 Budget]

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "And of course, the building plans must include a Hall of Traitors." [-1 Budget]

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: "I like your idea of converting this place into a Rizian History Museum." [-1 Budget]

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "Kidding about the Hall of Traitors, of course."

60.speaker: Lucita Azaro
60.text: "If that's what you want, then it's what I want too. Preserving our history will strengthen our future."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "However, as much as I'd like to include a Hall of Traitors, our current budget doesn't allow for it."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "I admit I like the idea of a wing showcasing the consequences of betrayal and disloyalty. Something to keep in mind for the future."

66.speaker: Player_Romus
66.text: "Thanks, but I’m not willing to spend anything on this. We need to find a more cost-effective solution."

67.speaker: Lucita Azaro
67.text: "Then why not just lock the door, board up the windows, and let nature take its course?"

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "Why didn't you start with that? Let’s do it."

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "Lock it up, board it up, and let the squirrels govern. I’m sure they’ll do a fine job."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "Let it slowly decay like all democratic movements that came before it."

72.speaker: Lucita Azaro
72.text: "Very well. Children are our future, after all."

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: The bells of the Archsanctuary of Zilba began to toll, as if sounding their approval of my decision.

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "Yes, enjoy the womb while you can. It's a cold, harsh world outside of it."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "Go home and get some rest. I'll meet up with you shortly."

77.speaker: Player_Romus
77.text: "Hopefully not too long. Your mother's turning into a real whale."

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: Her eyes softened with relief, and she offered me a smile.

80.speaker: Lucita Azaro
80.text: "A girl would never be this annoying."

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: She shot me a dirty look.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: I rang the golden bell with exaggerated reverence.

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "'Ladies and gentlemen, it is my privilege to call this meeting of the House of Delegates to order.'"

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: I pretended to hear enthusiastic applause from the vacant seats.

85.speaker: Player_Romus
85.text: "'Today we are humbled by the presence of His Majesty King Romus -- me. Long may he reign!'"

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: I gestured toward the empty seats as if acknowledging an imaginary cheer of “Long may he reign!”

87.speaker: Player_Romus
87.text: "'Today's session is regarding the proposal to shut down the House of Delegates."

88.speaker: Player_Romus
88.text: "The final decision is now in the hands of His Majesty King Romus."

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: I stepped away from the podium, standing in for the absent Delegates.

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "'Will you accept or overrule the Delegates' recommendation?'"

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: I glared out over the vacant seats, my tone shifting to harsh finality.

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "I will overrule it with pleasure. This House is dissolved.”

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: I rang the bell one last time, letting the sound resonate through the empty room.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: With a smirk, I raised it in a mock toast.

96.speaker: Player_Romus
96.text: "To the demise of this obsolete assembly. May its memory fade as swiftly as its relevance."

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: I took a sip from my flask before letting out a derisive chuckle.

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "To the end of pretenses and posturing."

100.speaker: Player_Romus
100.text: "To the end of farcical debates and the delusions of power!"

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: With that, I took a long drink from the flask, savoring the taste as if it were the last pleasure of the day.

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: I placed the flask back into my jacket with a satisfied nod, my eyes sweeping across the empty seats with disdain.

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: I rang the bell one final time, letting the sound resonate through the chamber.

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: I seized the golden bell and gave it a sharp ring, the sound piercing through the silence.

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "Ladies and gentlemen, I hereby end this farce."

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: I surveyed the vacant seats with cold disdain, the emptiness reflecting my contempt.

108.speaker: Player_Romus
108.text: "This charade of governance and debate has accomplished nothing but waste."

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: A bitter laugh escaped me, devoid of any real amusement.

110.speaker: Player_Romus
110.text: "Consider this your final lesson in irrelevance."

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: With a sudden, forceful motion, I hurled the bell across the room.

112.speaker: Narrator
112.text: It sailed through the air and struck a large, ornate vase on a pedestal, shattered into pieces upon impact.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: I turned on my heel, the sound of the vase’s destruction resonating as I walked away, leaving the chamber and its broken relics in my wake.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: I approached the podium with reverence and looked out over the vast emptiness of the chamber.

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: Taking a deep breath, I began with a prayer.

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "Lord, we seek Your insight as we navigate this moment of transformation.”

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: “Grant us wisdom to follow Your will."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: I paused, letting the silence settle before continuing.

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: “It is with a heavy heart that I reaffirm this assembly closed."

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "This chamber strayed from the path of righteousness.”

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: I gently placed my hand on the bell, a symbol of both the past and the future, before setting it aside.

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: I gave the bell a quick, decisive ring, the sound echoing through the room.

125.speaker: Player_Romus
125.text: "Let it be known that you had a good run, but it was time for a change."

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: I looked around the vacant seats.

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "The monarchy is supreme, and it is my duty to ensure its authority remains unchallenged.”

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "The promise of collective decision-making and the voice of the people was held within these walls."

129.speaker: Player_Romus
129.text: "Let this be a reminder that while institutions may come and go, the strength and unity of the Crown endure."

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: With a final glance around, I left the podium and turned away.

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "And now, the floor is open for debate!"

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "A quorum of one -- how efficient we've become."

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "What I'll accept is your undying loyalty. Henceforth, consider the House of Delegates no more."

134.speaker: Player_Romus
134.text: "The Crown's authority isn't meant to be shared. The House of Delegates is hereby disbanded, effective immediately."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: I rang the golden bell with a deliberate clang before reaching into my jacket and pulling out a flask.

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "To the final curtain call of a charade that never should have been."

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "To the end of an institution that failed to uphold the virtues it was meant to embody."

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "May the delusions of grandeur that plagued this place be as forgotten as the debates that never mattered."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "To the dissolution of a system that served only the privileged few!"

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "Let us toast to the closure of this pitiful attempt at governance!"

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "Here’s to the dissolution of empty rhetoric and self-important blunders!"

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: I took in the desolate room, feeling a strange sense of solitude.

156.text: "This abandoned hall is a stark reminder of the betrayal that unfolded within these walls."

157.speaker: Player_Romus
157.text: “This once-great assembly, now reduced to an empty shell, serves as a monument to your selfishness.

159.speaker: Player_Romus
159.text: "You were supposed to be champions of the people! Not a means to enrich yourselves on the backs of others."

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "You, who were entrusted with the greatest of responsibilities have squandered that trust."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "And now, it is I who stands victorious."

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: “And now, your dream of democratic ideals lay dead."

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: “As I stand before this once-great chamber, I am reminded of the noble intentions that guided its inception."

164.speaker: Player_Romus
164.text: It is undeniable that in its prime, this chamber symbolized the hopes and dreams of a society striving for progress."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "This space was designed to be a beacon of governance and representation."

166.speaker: Player_Romus
166.text: "We need Your strength more than ever."

167.speaker: Player_Romus
167.text: "May you fill our hearts with the Holy Spirit."

168.speaker: Player_Romus
168.text: "I ask for Your blessings, Lord, as we embark on this new chapter."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "As we stand on the brink of change, we turn to the heavens for guidance."

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: “The disbandment of this assembly is a necessary step towards reclaiming our principles."

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: The closure of this body signifies the removal of a stain on our governance."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "The delegates here opened themselves to the influence of wickedness."

173.speaker: Player_Romus
173.text: "This House of Delegates fell prey to the encroachment of evil."

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "May this decision bring us closer to the path of divine favor."

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "May all who have been part of this disbanded institution find forgiveness for their transgressions.”

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: “May the closure of this institution serve as a solemn reminder of our commitment to righteousness and justice.”

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "The Delegates who once filled these seats claimed to represent the people, but at the end of the day, they stood in defiance of the Crown’s will."

204.speaker: Hugo Toras
204.text: "Thanks to you, those voices have now been silenced."

205.speaker: Player_Romus
205.text: "They twisted our laws and traditions to suit their own purposes."

206.speaker: Player_Romus
206.text: "It pains me that it came to this, but I did what needed to be done."

207.speaker: Player_Romus
207.text: "I could not allow them to steer our kingdom off course."

208.speaker: Hugo Toras
208.text: "This empty chamber marks a new beginning."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "We will build something enduring. As Sovereign of this nation, I won't rest until my very last breath."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "The only question now... what do we do with this place?"

212.speaker: Hugo Toras
212.text: "We could turn it into an elite boarding school reserved for the children of Rizia's most powerful families."

213.speaker: Hugo Toras
213.text: "They’d be shaped and molded from a young age, their loyalty to their monarch unwavering."

214.speaker: Hugo Toras
214.text: “We’d ensure the next generation of leaders fully aligns with our vision for the kingdom.”

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "Now there's an idea! Cultivating the minds of the future right under our roof."

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "I don’t know… Children from powerful families can be hard to control. Am I right?"

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "Imagine the parents, clamoring to secure a spot for their precious offspring. We could make billions."

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: Hugo and I walked deeper into the chamber.

219.speaker: Hugo Toras
219.text: "What Porte Drazon lacks is a museum of Rizian history. A place dedicated to our kingdom's past -- a monument to our storied heritage."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "It would also be an opportunity to control the narrative by highlighting the legitimacy and necessity of my rule."

221.speaker: Hugo Toras
221.text: "Precisely. It will reinforce visitors' belief that your reign is the rightful path for our kingdom."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "What exactly did you have in mind?"

223.speaker: Hugo Toras
223.text: "Such an institution could trace the reign of House Toras, from its Rezenid-era beginnings to today."

224.speaker: Hugo Toras
224.text: “Reinforcing the message that our family's rule is the rightful path for this kingdom.”

225.speaker: Hugo Toras
225.text: "In any case, those are my thoughts. What are yours?"

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "A new beginning, yes. But it’s one that carries the weight of all we've sacrificed to get here."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "I believe founding an elite boarding school would best serve the kingdom." [-1 Budget]

228.speaker: Player_Romus
228.text: "I like your idea of turning this place into a Rizian History Museum." [-1 Budget]

229.speaker: Player_Romus
229.text: "Thanks for your ideas, but I’m not willing to spend much on this. We need to find a more cost-effective solution."

230.speaker: Hugo Toras
230.text: "It would cost little to nothing to simply lock the door, board up the windows, and let nature take its course."

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "Why didn't you lead with that? Let’s do it."

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "Board it up and let the squirrels govern. I’m sure they’ll manage just fine."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "Let this place slowly decay like all democratic movements that came before it."

235.speaker: Hugo Toras
235.text: "I think that's a wise decision. Educating the elite will ensure Rizia’s legacy."

236.speaker: Narrator
236.text: The nearby bells from the Archsanctuary of Zilba prompted Hugo to check his watch. He then looked up at me with a wry smile.

237.speaker: Hugo Toras
237.text: "I could not have said it better myself."

238.speaker: Player_Romus
238.text: "And let's go ahead and throw in that 'Hall of Traitors' you mentioned.” [-1 Budget]

242.speaker: Player_Romus
242.text: "Especially if a special wing is dedicated to showcasing the consequences of disloyalty and betrayal." [-1 Budget]

243.speaker: Player_Romus
243.text: “But I'm going to pass on your 'Hall of Traitors' idea. I'd rather the museum keep an upbeat tone."

244.speaker: Player_Romus
244.text: “But a wing dedicated to naming and shaming those who have betrayed me will have to wait until we have greater financial leeway.”

246.speaker: Player_Romus
246.text: "The House of Delegates was a place where the old order clung to power. Now, it’s ours to breathe new life into this kingdom."

248.speaker: Player_Romus
248.text: "We already have enough museums cluttering the city. Another one won’t change anything."

249.speaker: Player_Romus
249.text: "This hall, once filled with many voices, now stands as a testament to the Crown's true strength."

250.speaker: Hugo Toras
250.text: "History will remember this as the moment King Romus secured his place in Rizia's legacy."

251.speaker: Hugo Toras
251.text: "They didn't see the future you envisioned."

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "The Delegates who once resided in these seats claimed to represent the people, but at the end of the day, they stood in opposition to the Lord's will."

254.speaker: Sal Ignacius
254.text: "Indeed. God's justice will be served, and those who defied the Crown will face their due reckoning."

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "They distorted our laws and traditions to suit their own ends."

256.speaker: Player_Romus
256.text: "It’s difficult to accept that it came to this, but it needed to be done."

257.speaker: Player_Romus
257.text: "I couldn't allow them to lead our kingdom astray."

260.speaker: Player_Romus
260.text: "It thrives on chaos and pandering to the lowest common denominator."

261.speaker: Player_Romus
261.text: "Quixotic idealism fraught with manipulation, discord, and empty promises."

262.speaker: Player_Romus
262.text: "It's like handing a child a hammer -- everything becomes a nail ready to be smashed."

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: Sal smiled and placed a hand on my shoulder.

264.speaker: Sal Ignacius
264.text: "This hall may be empty now, but it marks a new beginning."

265.speaker: Player_Romus
265.text: "I'm determined to build something enduring. As Sovereign of this nation, I will not rest until my very last breath."

267.speaker: Sal Ignacius
267.text: "As it so happens, I've already given that question some consideration."

268.speaker: Sal Ignacius
268.text: "By moving the Council chambers here from Palas Rezna, we can open its sessions up to the public. Perhaps even hold televised services here on holidays."

269.speaker: Sal Ignacius
269.text: "This will engender a feeling of connection between the people of Rizia and their divinely appointed sovereign."

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "I like it. Rich or poor, noble or commoner, all who worship God shall be welcome in these halls."

271.speaker: Player_Romus
271.text: "Ambitious, but such a showy use of this building may provoke resistance from those who oppose our theocracy."

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "But if the chambers are moved from Palas Rezna, the Council will no longer be at my beck and call."

273.speaker: Sal Ignacius
273.text: "We could create a Museum of History. A place dedicated to Rizia’s past -- a symbol of national pride, and sacred heritage."

274.speaker: Player_Romus
274.text: "It could be an opportunity to control the narrative by highlighting the legitimacy of my rule."

275.speaker: Sal Ignacius
275.text: "My thoughts exactly. It would reinforce visitors' belief that your reign was ordained from above."

276.speaker: Player_Romus
276.text: “Why not create a Hall of Traitors --where the names and faces of all those who dared oppose me are prominently displayed?”

277.speaker: Sal Ignacius
277.text: "The Lord preaches forgiveness, Your Majesty. But if you believe such an showcase would keep your enemies at bay, I would support it."

278.speaker: Narrator
278.text: Sal paused, taking in the statues of our historic military figures that lined the hall.

279.speaker: Sal Ignacius
279.text: "Those are my ideas. But I believe you know my preference."

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "A new beginning, certainly. But it’s one that carries the weight of all we've sacrificed to get here."

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "The possibilities of what to do with this space are endless. I wouldn't know where to begin."

282.speaker: Player_Romus
282.text: "But enough talk. Let’s settle on what to do with this hollow hall of misrule."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "As you have requested, so it shall be. The Supreme Council of Nur will have a new home." [-1 Budget]

287.speaker: Player_Romus
287.text: "I’m in favor of transforming this place into a Rizian History Museum." [-1 Budget]

289.speaker: Player_Romus
289.text: "Thank you, but I’m reluctant to spend heavily on this. We need to look for more cost-efficient solutions."

290.speaker: Sal Ignacius
290.text: "You could simply lock the doors and board up the windows, letting nature take its course."

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: "Let it slowly decay like all democratic movements that came before it."

293.speaker: Sal Ignacius
293.text: "Praise the Lord! Rizia's faithful will be happy to hear of your choice."

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: The bells from the Archsanctuary of Zilba sounded, as if to mark the end of our deliberations. Sal glanced heavenward.

296.speaker: Sal Ignacius
296.text: "The people of Porte Drazon are bringing their dogs and cats to petition for their divine favor."

298.speaker: Player_Romus
298.text: "I see the bells are making a play for your attention."

299.speaker: Sal Ignacius
299.text: "I couldn’t have said it better myself."

300.speaker: Sal Ignacius
300.text: "It would be a great honor if you were to make an appearance."

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Complete with our very own Hall of Traitors."  [-1 Budget]

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: "Kidding, of course, about a Hall of Traitors."

306.speaker: Player_Romus
306.text: ""Especially if we add a wing devoted to highlighting the cost of betrayal and disloyalty." [-1 Budget]

307.speaker: Player_Romus
307.text: "However, as much as I'd like to include a Hall of Traitors, our budget doesn't allow for it."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "However, a wing highlighting the consequences of betrayal and disloyalty will need to wait until our finances improve."

310.speaker: Sal Ignacius
310.text: "An excellent choice. Protecting our sacred history will solidify our future."

311.speaker: Player_Romus
311.text: “The chambers reek of the last remnants of the old order desperately clinging to power."

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: “The Delegates who once occupied these seats never comprehended the true essence of eternal guidance and leadership.”

314.speaker: Player_Romus
314.text: "Museums don’t exactly stir the soul. What else do you have in mind?"

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "This desolate hall stands as a testament to the Crown's true strength."

316.speaker: Sal Ignacius
316.text: "Halaita. History will remember this as the moment King Romus secured his place in Rizia's blessed legacy."

317.speaker: Sal Ignacius
317.text: "They didn't see the future you've envisioned. But now, under Divine guidance, it’s yours to reshape -- to breathe new life into this kingdom."

318.speaker: Sal Ignacius
318.text: "Halaita. Divine wisdom far exceeds any earthly authority they ever imagined."

319.speaker: Player_Romus
319.text: “I’ll catch up with you shortly. I just need a bit more time here.”

321.speaker: Player_Romus
321.text: "As if you even had to ask."

322.speaker: Hugo Toras
322.text: “Great! Meet me in my study. I'll find an appropriate vintage for the occasion."

324.speaker: Narrator
324.text: He gave a slight bow before he turned and left.

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "Thanks, but I find the quiet here to be a welcome and much-needed respite."

326.speaker: Player_Romus
326.text: "The honor is mine. I'll meet up with you shortly."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "What? Of course! Bruno and I wouldn't miss it!"

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "I'll leave the grand appearances to you. I’m sure you have enough honor to spare for both of us."

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: He offered me an understanding smile before walking away.

330.speaker: Narrator
330.text: Sal forced a smile and gave a quick nod before walking away with a sharp, deliberate stride.

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: The wiseman smiled warmly and gave a respectful bow before he turned and left.

332.speaker: Sal Ignacius
332.text: "I'll see to it that the royal dog receives the most blessings of all."

334.speaker: Hugo Toras
334.text: "I don’t know about you, but as much as I enjoy scheming over what to do with the skeletal remains of this place, I could do with an aperitif.”

335.speaker: Hugo Toras
335.text: "It would be an honor if you joined me, even if only for a glass of water."

336.speaker: Hugo Toras
336.text: “I believe in the power of a restorative tipple to clear one's head after a long day. Perhaps it's old-fashioned of me."

337.speaker: Hugo Toras
337.text: "In any case, I will take my leave."

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "If it's a drink you want, I've got a flask right here."

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: I pulled out my flask from my jacket pocket and held it up.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: He took a quick swig before giving it back.

344.speaker: Hugo Toras
344.text: "Be careful, Your Majesty. Everything in moderation."

345.speaker: Narrator
345.text: It was difficult to discern whether there was a double meaning in his response.

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "Your timing for such an indulgence seems inappropriate, given the demands facing us."

350.speaker: Hugo Toras
350.text: “One can't spend all of one's time navigating those demands. It’s all about balance, after all!”

352.speaker: Sal Ignacius
352.text: "One answer stands out to me. This must be the home of the Supreme Council of Nur -- the body we created to replace the Royal Council."

353.speaker: Narrator
353.text: He looked at me, his eyes full of anticipation.

354.speaker: Sal Ignacius
354.text: "I must admit that such a hall feels a bit... heavy. But if you’re set on it, I’ll support the decision."

355.speaker: Sal Ignacius
355.text: "Oh, thank God! For a moment I'd thought you were serious."

356.speaker: Sal Ignacius
356.text: "To be honest, I can't say I was entirely supportive of that idea, but if it’s something you truly want down the line, I’m willing to back it."

357.speaker: Sal Ignacius
357.text: "I must take my leave. I'm due for our holy kingdom's first Blessing of the Pets."

358.speaker: Sal Ignacius
358.text: "Fair enough. Maybe it’s not the most exciting option, but I still think it has its merits."

359.speaker: Sal Ignacius
359.text: "I'm sorry you feel that way. In any case..."

360.speaker: Narrator
360.text: Sal paused, taking in the statues of our revered military figures that lined the hall.

361.speaker: Hugo Toras
361.text: "But we do not have one spotlighting the Royal Family and its lineage. One that cements the reign of House Toras in the public eye."

362.speaker: Hugo Toras
362.text: "I beg you not to dismiss this option so quickly. By building a museum, you will not only preserve history -- you will write it."

363.speaker: Narrator
363.text: He paused, taking in the statues of revered military figures that lined the hall.

364.speaker: Hugo Toras
364.text: "I couldn't agree more, Your Majesty. It would serve as a strong deterrent."

365.speaker: Hugo Toras
365.text: "I never called it that, Your Majesty. But I wholeheartedly approve."

366.speaker: Hugo Toras
366.text: "Understandable. However, if it’s something you truly want down the line, I’m willing to back it."

367.speaker: Player_Romus
367.text: "But enough talk. Let’s decide how to reclaim this hall of wasted voices, so we can move on with our lives."

369.speaker: Lucita Azaro
369.text: "'Noble' might be a bit too kind."

370.speaker: Lucita Azaro
370.text: "Precisely. That’s why it could never produce the kind of leadership this kingdom needs."

373.speaker: Lucita Azaro
373.text: "Visitors would leave believing that your reign -- *our* reign -- was the inevitable, rightful path for our kingdom."

374.speaker: Lucita Azaro
374.text: "Quite heavy-handed, but it would certainly underline the consequences for betraying the crown."

375.speaker: Lucita Azaro
375.text: "Ah, and here I was ready to start picking out the portraits."

376.speaker: Lucita Azaro
376.text: "Understandable. If it’s something you truly want down the line, we could certainly make it happen."

377.speaker: Lucita Azaro
377.text: "I know you're getting impatient, my prince. But you'll have to wait a little longer."

379.speaker: Player_Romus
379.text: "Go ahead. I'll join you soon. Just need a bit more time here."

380.speaker: Narrator
380.text: I took one final, contemplative look at the room.

382.speaker: Hugo Toras
382.text: “Alright. I’ll pour you a drink, but I can’t guarantee it’ll be there by the time you get to it.”

383.speaker: Hugo Toras
383.text: "Of course. Until then, I'll take my leave."

384.speaker: Narrator
384.text: After a moment, I nodded, feeling a sense of resolution, and then made my way out, with Hugo following close behind.

391.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
391.text: The location might not be ideal. A more fortified or secluded site could better serve as a strategic center.

392.speaker: Narrator
392.text: Better yet... a Hall of Traitors could be included -- where the names and faces of all those who resisted me are prominently displayed.

393.speaker: Narrator
393.text: Forever marked as disloyal. A strong reminder of where true power resides.

394.speaker: Narrator
394.text: Of course, a much less costly way to go would be to simply lock the door, board up the windows, and let nature take its course.

398.speaker: Player_Romus
398.text: "By royal decree, I hereby deem this chamber Rizia's premier boarding school!" [-1 Budget]

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "By royal decree, I hereby deem this chamber the new Rizian National History Museum!" [-1 Budget]

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: “By royal decree, by a 1-0 vote, I hereby deem this chamber indefinitely closed.”

404.speaker: Player_Romus
404.text: “By royal decree, I hereby order that any improvements to this chamber be deferred until our budget allows.”

405.speaker: Player_Romus
405.text: “By royal decree, I hereby condemn this chamber to slowly decay like all democratic movements that came before it."

409.speaker: Player_Romus
409.text: "Consider yourselves lucky that I won't include a Hall of Traitors!"

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.text: “But a wing dedicated to displaying the impact of your betrayal and disloyalty will be postponed until we have greater financial leeway.”

412.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
412.text: But museums were dull and might not draw many visitors. What would be the point if no one showed up?

413.speaker: Narrator
413.text: I paused, taking in the statues of revered military figures that lined the hall. Their presence stirred a thought...

414.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
414.text: It might be seen as a heavy-handed and provocative move.

416.speaker: Narrator
416.text: I gazed around the vacant hall and spoke to myself.

417.speaker: Player_Romus
417.text: "I will build something enduring and won't rest until my last breath."

418.speaker: Narrator
418.text: I wondered what to do with the building. It would be a shame to let it go to waste.

419.speaker: Narrator
419.text: I could turn this place into an elite boarding school reserved for the children of Rizia's most powerful families.

420.speaker: Narrator
420.text: Where they could be groomed from a young age, with their loyalty to the Crown never wavering.

421.speaker: Narrator
421.text: It would ensure the next generation of leaders fully aligned with my vision for the future.

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "I will bear the weight of all I've sacrificed to reach this point."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "Soon, my people will understand the guidance only a monarch can provide."

424.speaker: Narrator
424.text: I had no doubt that under my sole rule, Rizia would thrive.

429.speaker: Narrator
429.text: Unfortunately, our current budget didn't permit any renovations to the building.

430.speaker: Narrator
430.text: The only real choice I had was to lock the door, board up the windows, and let nature take its course.

431.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
431.text: I liked the idea, but there were other possibilities too.

433.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
433.text: Then again, my reign was far from over. Why focus on the past with so much future ahead of me?

434.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
434.text: But children from powerful families could be hard to control, if not managed properly.

435.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
435.text: But too much knowledge turns sheep into wolves, and livestock are easier to herd than thinkers.

436.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
436.text: Settle on a course of action.

437.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
437.text: Repurposing it might be seen as a loss of cultural heritage.

438.speaker: Narrator
438.text: I made several laps around the room, deep in thought, before a sudden clarity brought everything into focus.

439.speaker: Narrator
439.text: I walked over to the podium, standing behind it as if to address the nonexistent crowd.

440.speaker: Player_Romus
440.text: "Complete, of course, with a Hall of Traitors!” [-1 Budget]

441.speaker: Player_Romus
441.text: "In addition, a special wing will be dedicated to showcasing the consequences of my enemies' disloyalty and betrayal!" [-1 Budget]

442.speaker: Player_Romus
442.text: “By royal decree, I hereby condemn this chamber to a slow, unrelenting decay, much like all the democratic movements that came before it.”

446.speaker: Player_Romus
446.text: “By royal decree, I decree that this chamber shall stay as drab as a rainy day until we have more coins to jingle.”

447.speaker: Narrator
447.text: Mind racing with possibilities, I knew it was time to stop mulling it over and settle on a definitive course of action.

448.speaker: Narrator
448.text: We could turn this place into a Museum of History -- a monument dedicated to celebrating Rizia's heritage.

449.speaker: Narrator
449.text: My eyes fell on the constitution again. Seeing it sparked an idea...

450.speaker: Narrator
450.text: Not to mention, an opportunity to assert the legitimacy of my rule by controlling the narrative.

451.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
451.text: It might not have the impact I'm aiming for if it doesn't actively engage and attract visitors.

455.speaker: Narrator
455.text: With its fate decided, I took in the desolate room. The podium I was standing behind beckoned me to stay.

458.speaker: Player_Romus
458.text: "Then let us discuss dismantling this establishment to make room for an elite boarding school!"

460.speaker: Player_Romus
460.text: "I recommend shutting this assembly down for good because I hate you."

461.speaker: Player_Romus
461.text: "Ah, the sweet sound of obedience, ringing in every empty seat."

463.speaker: Player_Romus
463.text: "'Your Majesty, this proposal risks alienating the very citizens who have supported the Crown.'"

464.speaker: Player_Romus
464.text: "'But without the House of Delegates, how can we ensure that all perspectives are heard?"

465.speaker: Narrator
465.text: I paused, waiting for the silence to respond -- but unsurprisingly, it did not.

466.speaker: Narrator
466.text: I waited, but predictably, the silence offered no reply.

467.speaker: Player_Romus
467.text: "Let the minutes show… that there are no minutes to show."

468.speaker: Narrator
468.text: I looked around, hoping for some opposition. Instead, all I got was the soft creak of a door in the distance.

469.speaker: Narrator
469.text: The only response I got was the soft creak of a door in the distance.

473.speaker: Player_Romus
473.text: "Then let us discuss dismantling this establishment to make room for the Supreme Council of Nur!"

477.text: "Then let us discuss dismantling this establishment to make room for the Rizian History Museum!"

487.speaker: Player_Romus
487.text: "I regret to inform you that your services will no longer be required."

489.speaker: Player_Romus
489.text: "Oh no, not the citizens! Whatever shall we do without their impeccable judgment and boundless wisdom?"

490.speaker: Player_Romus
490.text: "Please... if they supported the Crown, they'd be thanking me for everything I've done for them."

491.speaker: Player_Romus
491.text: "From here on out, consider the House of Delegates no more."

492.speaker: Player_Romus
492.text: "Without their judgment, the House of Delegates is no longer necessary. Consider it dissolved permanently."

493.speaker: Player_Romus
493.text: "We'll thrive without their interference -- this assembly is dissolved."

494.speaker: Narrator
494.text: I straightened my back, clasping my hands behind me.

496.speaker: Narrator
496.text: I reverted to my role as king.

497.speaker: Player_Romus
497.text: "We don’t need a House of Delegates to hear voices that only sow dissent."

498.speaker: Player_Romus
498.text: "Sorry. I didn't quite get that. Try speaking a little louder next time."

499.speaker: Player_Romus
499.text: "Ensuring all perspectives? That's just another way to say 'invite havoc and surrender to anarchy.'"

500.speaker: Player_Romus
500.text: "This chamber will no longer house debates or dissent -- it ends here."

501.speaker: Player_Romus
501.text: "Consider the matter settled. The House of Delegates is permanently dissolved."

502.speaker: Player_Romus
502.text: "And with that, the House of Delegates is hereby disbanded, effective immediately."

503.speaker: Narrator
503.text: I straightened my back, clasping my hands firmly behind me.

504.speaker: Player_Romus
504.text: "'Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah!' That's all that ever came out of this hall!"

505.speaker: Narrator
505.text: I stepped away from the podium and left the chamber.

506.speaker: Player_Romus
506.text: "May its legacy remind us of our ongoing quest for a just and harmonious society.”

507.speaker: Player_Romus
507.text: "Perhaps in another era, under different circumstances, such democratic ideals may yet find their place and flourish."

508.speaker: Player_Romus
508.text: "I hope that eventually, my decision to close this institution will be viewed not as a betrayal, but as a step toward a greater vision for our kingdom."

509.speaker: Player_Romus
509.text: Farewell, to the House of Delegates. May the memory of what you aspired to be serve as a reminder of the ideals we strive to achieve."

513.speaker: Narrator
513.text: When I reached the chamber doors, I turned around.

514.speaker: Narrator
514.text: From here on out, I reigned alone.

516.speaker: Player_Romus
516.text: "Your time has passed, but you will be remembered."

529.speaker: Player_Romus
529.text: "Yes! A fitting end. Leave it to the mercy of the elements."

530.speaker: Lucita Azaro
530.text: "At least they'd be less nuts than the last lot we had in here."

534.speaker: Lucita Azaro
534.text: "A practical solution. Sometimes the simplest choice is the wisest."

535.speaker: Lucita Azaro
535.text: "The elements might show more mercy than some of the Delegates ever did."

536.speaker: Sal Ignacius
536.text: "Or, given the threats Rizia faces, perhaps transforming the building into a national defense headquarters is the right idea."

537.speaker: Sal Ignacius
